purpose: Vector store evaluation (#221, #230). One JSON per (vectors, arm, repetition) in the numbered directories; load1 files are the single-client load runs.

data.embedding_model: PE-Core-L14-336 image tower (open_clip, FP16, GPU 1), 1024-d, L2-normalized, the model the product serves
data.vectors: one whole-frame vector plus one crop vector per COCO ground-truth box (largest first, at most 12, shorter side at least 10 px); 6.5 vectors per image
data.held_out: 1300 images of the first 13600, never inserted: 1000 query vectors, 7299 vectors for the streaming-insert phase
data.sizes: 2,000 / 10,000 / 100,000: nested prefixes of the index set in a seeded image order (whole images stay together)
data.synthetic_fields: project (10 by image-id hash), class_validated 10%, test_holdout 5%, review_dismissed 2%, sel (uniform 0..9999); cluster_id is a 512-way spherical k-means of the index vectors; class_name is the COCO category
data.ground_truth: exact cosine top-100 per query per filter (numpy, CPU)
data.row_labels: every row is real embeddings; no noise-expanded or random vectors were used; 1M was not run

host.cpu: Intel Xeon E5-2680 v3 class, 48 threads, 503 GB RAM, NVMe
host.shared: yes: other projects ran on the host throughout; load average 10 to 195, whole-host CPU 25 to 100 percent busy; every phase records load before and after in its JSON
host.gpu: none attached to any engine; GPU 1 (RTX 3080 Ti) used only to generate the embeddings

engines.opensearch: opensearchproject/opensearch:3.6.0 @ sha256:b5dd1512af2a99748c942cfbbd7f32162623336b210667d0fc6333c6321f171d, 8 GB heap, 16 cores / 64 GB cgroup
engines.milvus: milvusdb/milvus:v2.6.25 @ sha256:29f7668e64df1c6d5cdadbfbee99f38c72e4001054f149a298725acae57230ad, standalone with embedded etcd and local storage
engines.lancedb: lancedb 0.40.0 embedded in the bench process (no cgroup limit; OMP/BLAS threads capped at 4)
engines.clients: opensearch-py 3.2.0, pymilvus 2.6.17, qdrant-client 1.19.1 (gRPC), psycopg 3.3.6, pgvector 0.5.1, faiss-cpu 1.15.1

protocol_deviations: Query repetitions are 3 per operating point inside a run; whole-arm repetitions: 3 (r1-r3) for the seven headline arms at 100,000, 1 for the secondary arms and the 2,000 / 10,000 rungs.
Query counts per point: 120 (sweep), 300 (detail), a smaller sample than the plan's 1000; recall values carry sampling error of a few thousandths.
One engine at a time, each arm in a fresh container; the rewrite, streaming and delete phases ran for the headline arms only.

Several runs of different arms overlapped in time by mistake (the process check used a filter that hid the running job): the 10,000 single-client load files and the 2,000 pgvector, LanceDB and flat files were re-run alone; the 100,000 LanceDB r3 was re-run alone. The first arms of the 10,000 rung may have overlapped with one LanceDB query run at 100,000; treat the 2,000 and 10,000 rungs as shape, not as precise latencies.
